name: Steel bucket
description: A galvanised steel pail with a wire bail. Holds water and can sit over a fire.
notes: The longest side is 1.28 times the reference's 250 mm and the box 3.9 times its volume because the bail stands up over the 220 mm pail; the pail itself is 250 mm across. cooking stands for the reference's boiling quality. The makeshift brazier is this bucket with holes punched in it, so it rides here.

name: Plastic bucket (5 gallon)
description: A large orange plastic bucket with a wire bail and grip. Holds about 19 litres.
notes: The pail is 365 mm tall, matching the reference's longest side; the bail standing up over it makes the model 504 mm tall, so the longest side reads 1.36 times the reference. The box is 2 times the reference volume for the same reason. No cooking quality: it is plastic.

name: Wooden bucket
description: A bucket carved from one block of hardwood, with a wooden crossbar handle. Holds about 5 litres.
notes: The reference has no longest side; 260 by 350 mm with the handle fits its 7.5 L. The box is 3.2 times the reference volume because the handle stands above the open pail. Mostly a crafted item, so its loot economy is thin.

name: Drink can
description: An empty 355 ml aluminium drink can with its ring-pull tab.
notes: The tin can variants ride here as the reference groups them, but the existing empty_can model (a steel tin with a paper label) fits can_food and can_medium better, and the 3 L can_food_big and the hobo stove would each read better with a model of their own. A lid that is pulled open has no item state.

name: Cardboard tube
description: An empty cardboard core from a roll of tape or paper.
notes: CHECK VOLUME (x29): the reference's 6 ml is the cardboard, not the open tube a player sees, which is 42 mm across and 100 mm long. The tube is hollow and lies on its side. Category material because it is crafting stock rather than a container.

name: Clay cup
description: A thick-walled fired clay beaker. Holds about half a litre and stands in a fire.
notes: A plain handleless beaker in clay-terracotta, 120 mm tall to match the reference's longest side. Mostly a crafted item, so its loot economy is thin.

name: Condom
description: A latex condom. Stretches to hold a little water.
notes: Modelled as the square foil wrapper with the rolled ring pressing through it, the shape a player recognises; a loose rolled ring 30 mm across would not read in the world. The ring is brass against the foil-gold wrapper so it shows. The sealed condom and the balloon ride here; a balloon would read better with its own model. Holding water has no content field yet.

name: Foil cup
description: A small cup folded from kitchen foil. Holds water and can be set on coals.
notes: CHECK VOLUME (x71): the reference's 5 ml is the folded foil, not the open cup, which is 80 mm across and 55 mm tall. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy. Vertical folds and a turned-over lip mark it as folded rather than pressed.

name: Plastic cup
description: A thin disposable white plastic cup.
notes: White so the yoghurt pot and the styrofoam cup can ride on it.

name: Trauma kit pouch
description: A zipped fabric pouch for a personal trauma kit, with webbing straps to mount it on a belt or vest.
notes: Coyote cloth-canvas body with cord-olive webbing, two red pull tabs and a red cross patch. An olive drab cloth finish would suit the military look better. The pocket grid is a placeholder, and mounting on a vest has no content field yet.

name: Police first aid pack
description: A vacuum-sealed pack of bleeding control supplies carried by patrol officers. Open it to get the contents.
notes: Modelled sealed: a black vacuum pouch drawn over a bandage roll, welded at both ends, with a white label and red cross. Its contents and the opening action wait on the refactor.

name: Glass jar (0.5 L)
description: A half-litre glass canning jar with a screw band and a flat lid. Keeps food sealed.
notes: The jar is hollow glass-clear; the tiles draw it opaque, but it stays see-through in the game. The 3 L jar and the cream jars ride here as the reference groups them, though at 3 to 3.85 L they are much larger; the preserved brain would read better with contents drawn in the jar.

name: Plastic jerrycan
description: A red 10 litre plastic fuel can with a carry handle and a capped spout.
notes: The steel jerrycan (26.75 L) and the gallon can ride here as the reference groups them; the steel can would read better with its own pressed-steel model. Holding fuel has no content field yet.

name: Aluminium keg
description: A reusable 50 litre aluminium beer keg with a valve in the top and hand holes in its upper rim.
notes: 400 mm across and 530 mm tall, which fits the reference's 50 L. The steel keg shares the shape. The 60 L tank also fits, but the 2 L tank would read better with its own model. The size is a placeholder for a thing too big to carry far.

name: Propane cylinder (45 kg)
description: A tall white steel cylinder of propane with a brass valve under a guard collar. Used for heating and cooking.
notes: A 100 pound cylinder, 370 mm across and 1170 mm tall to match the reference's longest side. The reference files it as a tool magazine holding gas; fuel charges and connecting it to a heater have no content field yet. The handwheel is black plastic for the reference's plastic material. The size is a placeholder for a thing too big to carry far.
